3. **P2 — Google and Microsoft code exchanges omit the PKCE verifier.**  
   [Google oauth.ex:48](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_google/lib/jido_connect/google/oauth.ex:48), [Microsoft oauth.ex:48](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_microsoft/lib/jido_connect/microsoft/oauth.ex:48)

   Both authorization helpers accept `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method`. Neither token exchange includes `code_verifier`, even when the caller supplies it. Captured request bodies confirmed the omission for both providers.

   A PKCE exchange requires this verifier. [RFC 7636, section 4.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7636.txt) Existing exchange tests do not check this field. **Correction:** include the optional verifier in the exchange form and test the outgoing request. The host must continue to own verifier storage.

Acceptance: Reproduce the reported case against current source, apply the smallest correction described above, and add focused verification of both the failing case and supported behavior. For documentation/design work, update the public contract and verify its examples/callers. Preserve tenant, scope, lease, and host ownership boundaries. Use fresh matching v3 dependencies for final verification; saved local v2 build artifacts do not establish v3 conformance.

Do not modify jido_mcp or publish packages. Full source review and its coverage/verification limits are preserved in the parent epic comments.
